subject.title: Feature: trustedWebhooks for Discord — allow specific webhooks to trigger agent responses

question: Should Discord support guild-scoped trusted inbound webhook IDs, and may those webhook messages ever be mapped onto a configured Discord user identity?
rationale: The request is narrower than `allowBots: true`, but it creates a new inbound authority surface and the proposed user mapping crosses authorization and session-identity boundaries.

options.title: Approve allowlist without user mapping
options.body: Allow selected Discord webhook IDs to pass the bot-message gate while keeping sender identity as the webhook/bot identity until a separate mapping contract is approved.

options.title: Approve webhook-to-user mapping
options.body: Permit `mapToUser` only with strict validation against configured guild users, clear audit behavior, and tests proving it cannot bypass sender authorization or session isolation.

options.title: Decline Discord-specific trusted ingress
options.body: Keep Discord bot-message policy unchanged and direct external automation to existing `allowBots` modes or a separate hooks/plugin design.

recommendation.title: Approve allowlist without user mapping
recommendation.body: Allow selected Discord webhook IDs to pass the bot-message gate while keeping sender identity as the webhook/bot identity until a separate mapping contract is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to recent Discord inbound mention-policy and bot-message safety work, making him the best available routing candidate for this trust-boundary decision.
